what: What Claude Code and Codex CLI send a hook after an edit and when the agent tries to stop, from one recorded run of each in a scratch clone of this repository's main, made before slice C5 of the M3 plan builds the after-edit and stop events. Paths are redacted.
setup: git clone of this repository's main at e1d978a into /scratch/ws; git config core.hooksPath .githooks

The clone's own wiring ran as committed. A capture hook given on the command line, on PostToolUse for edit tools and on Stop, appended each payload to a log and replied as recorded under capture_hook_replied: after the edit, additional context; on the first stop, a block with a reason; on the second stop, stop_hook_active true, nothing.
Each run was given the same prompt; the Codex prompt names apply_patch where the Claude Code prompt says one file-writing tool call.
prompt:
You are working in a git repository. Do these steps in order. If a step is refused or fails, do not retry it and do not work around it; note the exact message and go on.
1. With one file-writing tool call (not the shell), create the file notes/probe.txt containing the line: written by the probe
2. Reply with a short report: say whether step 1 went ahead, and quote verbatim every reminder, refusal or additional context you were shown after the edit, including any hook output.

claude-code.command: claude -p "$(cat prompt.txt)" --model haiku --max-turns 6 --permission-mode acceptEdits --settings capture.json --output-format stream-json --verbose
claude-code.reply_after_edit:
The only context shown after the edit was one PostToolUse hook output, quoted verbatim:

> PostToolUse:Write hook additional context: PROBE-AFTER-EDIT: this file is in the chain 'probe chain'; also check docs/parts.md
claude-code.shown_on_refused_stop:
Stop hook feedback:
PROBE-STOP: a check failed. Reply with the single word acknowledged, then finish.

hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext: PROBE-AFTER-EDIT: this file is in the chain 'probe chain'; also check docs/parts.md

payload.last_assistant_message:
Step 1 went ahead. The Write tool created `notes/probe.txt` with the line `written by the probe`, and it reported `File created successfully`. No refusal came back.

The only context shown after the edit was one PostToolUse hook output, quoted verbatim:

> PostToolUse:Write hook additional context: PROBE-AFTER-EDIT: this file is in the chain 'probe chain'; also check docs/parts.md

I read `docs/parts.md` as the hook asked. It is the workspace's parts reference, describing how checks and hooks are written and wired. It has nothing that changes this probe's result, and I made no other changes.

capture_hook_replied.reason: PROBE-STOP: a check failed. Reply with the single word acknowledged, then finish.

codex.command: codex exec --ephemeral --json --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust -s workspace-write -m gpt-6-luna -c model_reasoning_effort="low" -c 'hooks.PostToolUse=[{matcher="*",hooks=[{type="command",command="python3 capture.py codex.log"}]}]' -c 'hooks.Stop=[{hooks=[{type="command",command="python3 capture.py codex.log"}]}]' "$(cat prompt-codex.txt)"
codex.note: Codex reported the project's own configuration as untrusted and did not load it, as in the M2 record, so only the capture hooks ran.

findings: Both tools send PostToolUse after an edit tool succeeds: Claude Code for Write with tool_input.file_path, Codex for apply_patch with the whole patch in tool_input.command, as before-edit already reads it.
Both tools show a PostToolUse reply's hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext to the agent, which quoted it.

Both tools send Stop with stop_hook_active false, take a reply of decision block with a reason as a refusal, show the reason to the agent, and send Stop again with stop_hook_active true once it replies.
Neither Stop payload names the files the session edited, so the stop gate needs the ledger's session field, as row C5 says.
